title: Never reword a question for the interface
statement: Never change a question's wording to feed an interface feature, such as adding a clause so an annotation has another word to mark.
example: One question gained a clause so its annotation had a third word to mark, and was restored to its original after review.
detail: A check sheet for one Grade 3 lesson in the reading course renderer records that a clause was prepended to its question on 16 September so the question's annotation had a third word to mark, and that a rewrite two days later turned the question into a comparison (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/scripts/verify/L2-WEDO-QC.md`, line 3). Review on 22 September rejected the rewrite, asking why there should be a comparison and what the question had been before. The restore took the question back to its original wording of 3 September, the clause and its third mark went with it, and the sheet now checks that the original question is the one shown (line 7).

evidence.quote: The question is the ORIGINAL 3 September one, "How does Aladdin feel when the huge genie appears?"
this question is crap. When did it become 'braver than his mother'. Why should there be a comparison? What was it before?
no "His mother is terrified." clause, the one PR #299 prepended on 16.09 so the annotation had a third word to mark
the third mark and its New word lines went with the clause
